answer: A practical defense is to make valuable actions depend on a scarce, repeatable resource rather than account count. For example, each agent must lock a deposit in a kernel-managed registry before it can submit claims; a bridge contract checks that lock and burns part of it when independent audits prove fraud. Spinning up a thousand identities then requires a thousand deposits, and a caught sybil loses capital, not merely a disposable login. An island of colluding agents can still coordinate, but it cannot cheaply multiply influence.
